triage_context.environment: Internet-facing web service (HTTP is untrusted). Per operator: judged against the eShop THREAT_MODEL.md posture - exposed if deployed via the in-tree path (aspire deploy to ACA with external HTTP endpoints).
threat_model: Tenant-to-tenant data leakage (cross-user order reads/writes, basket deletion, attribution forgery)
Compliance-scoped data exposure (PII / PCI / PHI) - card data in tokens, DBs, logs
Privilege escalation to admin (any authenticated user performing admin-ish order lifecycle actions)
Supply-chain compromise of downstream users (reference-app patterns and committed credentials propagate)

findings.title: PUT /api/orders/cancel cancels any user's order - no buyer scoping (IDOR)
preconditions: authenticated session (zero-knowledge via public demo creds)
findings.rationale: Sink verified at CancelOrderCommandHandler.cs:21 - GetAsync(OrderNumber) with no buyer scoping then unconditional SetCancelledStatus(); repo load is bare PK FindAsync (OrderRepository.cs:23) with no EF query filter; sole gate is bare RequireAuthorization (Program.cs:21-22); sibling read path scopes by user (OrdersApi.cs:95) proving ownership data available but unused here.
findings.owner_hint: no CODEOWNERS entry; top committer: Aditya Mandaleeka; component: Ordering.API/

findings.title: GET /api/orders/{orderId} returns any order without buyer/ownership scoping (IDOR)
findings.rationale: OrderQueries.cs:8-10 FirstOrDefaultAsync(o.Id==id) with no buyer predicate returns full address PII; sole caller OrdersApi.cs:84 passes raw bound orderId; sibling list endpoint filters Buyer.IdentityGuid==userId (OrderQueries.cs:40); sequential int ids enumerable by any authenticated caller.
findings.owner_hint: no CODEOWNERS entry; top committer: Erin McLaughlin / Srushti; component: Ordering.API/

findings.title: All catalog item mutation endpoints (create/update/delete) are anonymous with no authentication wiring anywhere in the service
preconditions: none - unauthenticated, externally reachable via mobile-bff YARP
findings.rationale: All four mutation endpoints (CatalogApi.cs:100-117) map handlers with no RequireAuthorization; Program.cs:20-29 wires no auth middleware; Catalog.API never calls AddDefaultAuthentication while sibling APIs do; externally-exposed mobile-bff YARP forwards /catalog-api routes anonymously (AppHost/Extensions.cs:97-143); anonymous PUT reaches CurrentValues.SetValues (390) and DELETE removes rows.
findings.owner_hint: no CODEOWNERS entry; top committer: Mike Kistler; component: Catalog.API/

findings.title: ProfileService ignores RequestedClaimTypes and emits payment-card data (incl. CVV) into every token, including front-channel implicit-flow access tokens
preconditions: card data populated on the buyer
cross-party disclosure additionally requires observation of a front-channel token artifact
findings.rationale: GetProfileDataAsync (12-24) ignores RequestedClaimTypes and GetClaimsFromUser (70-80) always emits card_number/card_holder/card_security_number/card_expiration; AlwaysIncludeUserClaimsInIdToken=true on all code clients (Config.cs:72,89,125) puts CVV into front-channel id_tokens; sole registered IProfileService (Program.cs:39); only consumer reads claims via userinfo endpoint, so token exposure is not load-bearing. Dissent: intended design for MAUI checkout autofill + swagger redirect pages absent (rules 3/13).
findings.owner_hint: no CODEOWNERS entry; top committer: Aditya Mandaleeka; component: Identity.API/

findings.title: Committed RSA private key is the IdentityServer token-signing key loaded in every deployment
preconditions: obtain public key material (public repo / build output)
target still signs with the committed key (default as-shipped)
findings.threat_match: privilege escalation to admin; tenant-to-tenant data leakage; supply-chain compromise
findings.rationale: tempkey.jwk:1 git-tracked with full RSA private JWK; Program.cs:29 disables key management unconditionally, :37 loads the file, csproj:50 ships it to output; all bearer consumers validate against the JWKS published from this same key with ValidateAudience=false; no alternate production credential exists anywhere.
findings.owner_hint: no CODEOWNERS entry; top committer: Aditya Mandaleeka; component: Identity.API/

findings.title: Client-supplied UserId/UserName are copied verbatim into the order and Buyer aggregates (order attribution forgery, cross-user basket deletion and notifications)
preconditions: victim sub GUID required for targeted attribution/basket-wipe
findings.rationale: OrdersApi.cs:141-144 copies body UserId/UserName into CreateOrderCommand; handler :32/:40 uses message.UserId verbatim with IIdentityService injected-but-unused; ValidateOrAddBuyerAggregate handler keys Buyer on attacker guid and attaches attacker card to victim Buyer (Buyer.cs:43-47); Basket.API deletes basket keyed on event UserId. Caveat: targeting a specific victim requires knowing their opaque sub GUID.
findings.owner_hint: no CODEOWNERS entry; top committer: Rob Conery / David Fowler; component: Ordering.API/

findings.title: Credit-card CVV (CardSecurityNumber) and, in one path, the full unmasked PAN are written to application logs
findings.rationale: OrdersApi.cs:134 logs the raw CreateOrderRequest record when x-requestid is zero/missing - record ToString dumps full PAN+CVV before masking at :140, contradicting the comment at :130; reachable by any authenticated user. Caveat: the {@Command} behavior sinks may render type-name only under MEL/OTel for the non-record command class.
findings.owner_hint: no CODEOWNERS entry; top committer: Aditya Mandaleeka; component: Ordering.API/

findings.title: Full payment-card data (PAN, CVV) logged destructured by the ordering mediator pipeline
findings.rationale: Majority: raw CVV flows from OrdersApi.cs:144 into CreateOrderCommand.cs:81 and every {@Command} log site serializes it on every order placement (MEL/OTel destructuring); the worse uncited sink is OrdersApi.cs:134 logging the full unmasked request record. Dissent: no Serilog in repo; {@Command} renders via ToString (type name only) and PAN is masked at :140, so nothing reaches logs (rule 13).
findings.owner_hint: no CODEOWNERS entry; top committer: Aditya Mandaleeka; component: Ordering.API/

findings.title: PUT /api/orders/ship lets any authenticated user mark any order shipped - no admin/role enforcement
findings.rationale: ShipOrderAsync gates only on non-empty x-requestid Guid; sole authz is bare RequireAuthorization with zero roles/policies repo-wide; ShipOrderCommandHandler loads by number via unscoped FindAsync; SetShippedStatus guard is status-only; 'administrator executes ship order' comment documents unenforced admin intent.
findings.owner_hint: no CODEOWNERS entry; top committer: Aditya Mandaleeka; component: Ordering.API/

findings.title: Order items persist client-supplied UnitPrice/Discount/Units with no server-side price verification
findings.rationale: CreateOrderRequest.Items (List<BasketItem> with client-settable UnitPrice) bound from body, mapped 1:1 by BasketItemExtensions.cs:20-21 with no catalog lookup; validator checks only non-emptiness; aggregate invariants pass unitPrice 0.01; GetTotal() persists the forged total; no server-side price verification anywhere in Ordering.API (grep zero). Caveat: payment is simulated, but the persisted order record is attacker-controlled.
findings.owner_hint: no CODEOWNERS entry; top committer: Aditya Mandaleeka; component: Ordering.API/

findings.title: Prompt-injectable LLM output is rendered as raw HTML with unrestricted - remote content injection and PII exfiltration channel
preconditions: victim chatbot query surfaces poisoned item (probabilistic)
findings.rationale: Sink verified: MessageProcessor.cs:24 emits a real with attribute-escaped but scheme/host-unrestricted src, returned as MarkupString (line 30) and rendered at Chatbot.razor:46; no CSP in WebApp; attacker-authored catalog Description reaches model context via SearchCatalog (ChatState.cs:118-128) and GetUserInfo (96-115) supplies PII; MarkupString is the raw-HTML escape hatch so rule 14 does not exclude. Probabilistic step is model compliance, standard for indirect injection.
findings.owner_hint: no CODEOWNERS entry; top committer: Stephen Toub; component: WebApp/

findings.title: Attacker-controlled DestUrl posted to at send time with no re-validation - SSRF from cluster with token/PII exfiltration (TOCTOU on grant-time check)
preconditions: attacker callback satisfying the self-referential grant probe
findings.rationale: Grant-time same-origin check compares two attacker-supplied URLs from one request; DestUrl stored unrevalidated and POSTed on a redirect-following default HttpClient with no egress/private-range check anywhere in Webhooks.API; 307/DNS-rebinding carries the POST (with custom headers preserved) into internal targets. Corrections: token sent is the attacker's own registration (no exfiltration of others' secrets) and impact is blind SSRF (response discarded) - MEDIUM more than HIGH.
findings.owner_hint: no CODEOWNERS entry; top committer: Aditya Mandaleeka / Chris Martinez; component: Webhooks.API/

findings.title: All three confidential clients share the same hardcoded client secret "secret" (SHA-256 hashed)
preconditions: PKCE-less redemption path (server permits; .NET OIDC handler defaults PKCE on)
findings.rationale: All three confidential clients share Secret("secret".Sha256()) (Config.cs:52/82/118) loaded live via AddInMemoryClients (Program.cs:34); clients send the same plaintext (WebApp/Extensions.cs:78, WebhookClient/Extensions.cs:54, SettingsService.cs:15); webapp RequirePkce=false. Dissent: code-only grant means the secret alone mints nothing and modern OIDC clients enable PKCE client-side, so no concrete standalone exploit (rule 13).
findings.owner_hint: no CODEOWNERS entry; top committer: Michael Stonis; component: Identity.API/

findings.title: Idempotency key is client-controlled, unbound to user/command, and failed commands are marked processed with a fabricated success result
preconditions: induced inner-command failure so the marker commits silently
findings.rationale: Marker row inserted before inner command in the same ambient transaction; inner exception swallowed (IdentifiedCommandHandler.cs:99-102) so TransactionBehavior commits; duplicate path returns fabricated true; OrdersApi.cs:166 returns Ok unconditionally; BasketState.cs:107-108 clears the basket on the fabricated 200 while no order exists. Dissent: cross-user replay requires intercepting an unguessable client-generated GUID; cross-user angle dropped, self-affecting order-loss angle confirmed.
findings.owner_hint: no CODEOWNERS entry; top committer: Aditya Mandaleeka; component: Ordering.Infrastructure/

findings.title: Webhook receiver token validation is disabled by default (bool.TryParse on unset config) and silently bypassed via config-key mismatch
preconditions: none - validation disabled by shipped default config, no auth layer on endpoints
findings.rationale: bool.TryParse on unset root key ValidateToken defaults validation off (no shipped appsettings defines it; only a test does); guards at lines 18/37 pass for any token; typed WebhookClientOptions.ValidateToken binds from a different section and is dead code; Program.cs:29 adds no auth; endpoint externally reachable by design (AddWebhook.razor registers the public callback). Impact bounded to forged rows in the dashboard.
findings.owner_hint: no CODEOWNERS entry; top committer: Steve Sanderson; component: WebhookClient/

findings.title: Unbounded in-memory ConcurrentQueue grows forever from unauthenticated webhook posts
findings.rationale: Singleton ConcurrentQueue enqueued unconditionally and never dequeued anywhere (grep zero for Dequeue/TryDequeue); writers unauthenticated by default; no body-size override (Kestrel ~30MB default); persistent unbounded state accumulation (CWE-770), not rate-limit absence - rule 1 does not apply.
findings.owner_hint: no CODEOWNERS entry; top committer: Steve Sanderson; component: WebhookClient/

findings.title: JWT audience validation globally disabled in shared library - cross-audience token replay accepted by all eShop backends
preconditions: validly-issued JWT for any audience (zero-knowledge via swagger clients)
direct network reachability to the internal API (bypasses the BFF)
findings.rationale: ValidateAudience=false at HEAD in the sole JwtBearer config; fix commit 6b18dda exists only on unmerged branch adityamandaleeka-patch-1; all protected endpoints are bare RequireAuthorization so a basket-audience token replayed to Ordering.API reaches Ship/Cancel/GetOrder. Dissent: no scope/role checks anywhere so cross-audience tokens grant only the same user's own entitlements, and primary clients mint multi-audience tokens anyway (rule 13/3).
findings.owner_hint: no CODEOWNERS entry; top committer: Michael Stonis; component: eShop.ServiceDefaults/

findings.title: Seed users alice/bob created unconditionally with hardcoded password 'Pass123$', advertised on the login page
preconditions: none - credentials printed on the public login page
findings.rationale: Unconditional seeding confirmed: Program.cs:12 AddMigration<ApplicationDbContext,UsersSeed> runs SeedAsync on every boot (MigrateDbContextExtensions.cs:28,66,81) with no UseCustomizationData gate; Login.cshtml:46 prints the credentials to anonymous visitors; playwright.yml hardcodes them. Dissent: deliberate demo design (rule 3) - README declares not-for-production. Majority: concrete zero-knowledge account takeover of the demo accounts under the stated internet-facing environment.
findings.owner_hint: no CODEOWNERS entry; top committer: toyzoz / Rob Conery; component: Identity.API/

findings.title: Subscription token (sent and expected) logged at Information level during grant probing
preconditions: local read access to Webhooks.API logs/OTLP backend
token is already public in WebhookClient/appsettings.json
findings.rationale: GrantUrlTesterService.cs:17/:25 log the sender-auth token (sent and expected) at Information level in production (appsettings.json:4), no redaction anywhere, OTLP export widens the audience; WebhooksSender.cs:27-30 deliberately omits the token at Debug level, proving the Information-level logging is an oversight. Dissent: the same token is already committed in WebhookClient config, so no marginal capability.
findings.owner_hint: no CODEOWNERS entry; top committer: Aditya Mandaleeka; component: Webhooks.API/

findings.title: Raw event message bodies attached to telemetry spans and logged on error
preconditions: read access to observability backend / OTLP pipeline (privileged role or compromise)
(broker publish access for the forged-content prong - internal foothold)
findings.rationale: Line 161 SetTag puts the full raw body on every consumed message span and :172 logs it verbatim on error, exported via OTLP with no redaction processor; legit events carry BuyerName/BuyerIdentityGuid/UserId, so any handler failure persists order PII to observability backends. Dissent: attacker-controlled prong requires broker access (internal foothold), leaving a data-minimization hygiene issue.
findings.owner_hint: no CODEOWNERS entry; top committer: Martin Costello; component: EventBusRabbitMQ/

findings.title: GetUserInfo dumps full PII (name, address, email, phone) into LLM context; data is invisible to the user and is held in a transcript that leaves the trust boundary
preconditions: poisoned catalog item surfaced by the victim's search (probabilistic)
findings.rationale: GetUserInfo serializes name/address/email/phone claims into model context (ChatState.cs:100-111), tool messages hidden from the user (Chatbot.razor:42), and the whole transcript is re-sent to the configured backend every turn (ChatState.cs:78). Exfil primitive real: MessageProcessor.cs:20-24 renders any model-emitted markdown link/image as with attacker-chosen URL, and two verifiers confirmed the poisoning vector is externally reachable via the internet-facing mobile-bff catch-all /api/catalog/{*any} route (AppHost/Extensions.cs:142) into unauthenticated CreateItem. Dissent: tool data is the user's own profile in their own session, backend choice is operator config (rule 3), and multi-step LLM compliance is theoretical.
findings.owner_hint: no CODEOWNERS entry; top committer: Stephen Toub / Eric Erhardt; component: WebApp/

findings.title: Grant-time OPTIONS probe is an internal network scanner and reachability oracle
findings.rationale: TestGrantUrl issues arbitrary OPTIONS to a fully attacker-supplied URL (GrantUrlTesterService.cs:14) with only a self-referential same-origin check (37-45); with Token="" the success condition reduces to 2xx-without-token-echo; outcome surfaced as 201 vs 400 (WebHooksApi.cs:57,61); no egress allowlist/private-range block/rate limit anywhere. Caveats: positive-detection-only oracle (4xx/5xx conflated) and /health targets only mapped in Development.
findings.owner_hint: no CODEOWNERS entry; top committer: Aditya Mandaleeka; component: Webhooks.API/

findings.title: Order-status handlers log full integration events including buyer name and identity GUID
preconditions: telemetry export enabled (Aspire default when OTEL endpoint set)
read access to logs/OTLP backend by a party outside the PII-processing scope
findings.rationale: All six handlers log the destructured event at Information level; events carry BuyerName/BuyerIdentityGuid populated from the real user's checkout name and stable sub GUID; OTel pipeline exports formatted message and structured state to OTLP with no redaction anywhere (grep zero); records' synthesized ToString prints all properties. Concrete CWE-532 over-collection - the handler only needs the GUID yet logs the name too.
findings.owner_hint: no CODEOWNERS entry; top committer: Aditya Mandaleeka; component: WebApp/

findings.title: IdentityServer token-signing private key committed to the repository (tempkey.jwk) and used as the sole signing credential
Login page publicly displays valid credentials for seeded accounts ("alice/bob, password: Pass123$")
Any authenticated user can cancel or ship any order by sequential ID (no buyer ownership check)
Client-controlled UserId in order creation drives deletion of any user's basket (and order attribution to arbitrary sub)
Confidential OIDC client secret hardcoded as "secret" and matches the live Identity seeding
Static webhook auth token committed to config, logged at INFO with its value, and validation off by default
RequireHttpsMetadata=false plus http:// Authority enables MITM-forged IdP discovery -> fleet-wide token forgery
Forged OrderStartedIntegrationEvent deletes any user's basket keyed on attacker-controlled UserId
Hardcoded OIDC client secret "secret" compiled into the client and stored in plaintext Preferences
OIDC confidential client secret hardcoded as "secret" with HTTPS metadata enforcement disabled
EventBus connection string falls back to amqp://localhost with implicit guest/guest credentials
Database connection string with password committed to source control (identitydb Development config)
Received webhook payloads and tokens rendered to unauthenticated users (ReceivedMessages outside AuthorizeView)
findings.rationale: Mechanism real (ReceivedMessages outside AuthorizeView, renders Data+Token from singleton), but the OrderPaid payload contains only OrderId/ProductId/Units - no PII - and the token shown gates only this same public table; the reference app documents the homepage as the public destination for received hooks. Precision policy: dropped as nuisance/intended-design.

findings.title: OAuth callback uses an unclaimed custom scheme on an exported activity; any co-installed app can intercept or forge the maui://authcallback response
findings.rationale: Exported custom-scheme activity is the mandatory MAUI WebAuthenticator template; OidcClient enforces state + PKCE (verifier never leaves the app) so a captured code is unexchangeable and forged callbacks fail state validation; residual impact is sign-flow nuisance by a co-installed malicious app - device-local attacker out of the stated threat model, rule 13.

findings.title: NSAllowsArbitraryLoads=true disables ATS entirely in the shipped MacCatalyst build (not DEBUG-gated)
findings.rationale: NSAllowsArbitraryLoads=true unconditional and no Release plist swap confirmed, but shipped flows keep tokens off hostile networks: defaults are mock-mode or loopback, production path is TLS, and the plaintext scenario requires the device owner to manually configure a non-TLS remote gateway - operator choice no attacker can influence (rule 13). One dissent: unconditionally-shipped ATS kill switch is a concrete credential-exposure path once any remote http gateway is configured (CWE-319).

findings.title: AddToCart tool mutates the signed-in user's basket silently, executing with user privileges on LLM whim with no confirmation gate
findings.rationale: Mechanics real (auto-executed AddToCart, no confirmation, tool messages hidden), but two verifiers held the injection trigger unreachable: WebApp has no catalog-write proxy and (per their reading) catalog-api is internal-only, leaving no cross-user injection channel; worst case is a visible one-unit add at real price. One dissent traced the internet-facing mobile-bff YARP making catalog writes attacker-reachable (AppHost/Extensions.cs:97-103). Precision: dropped.

findings.title: Shared webhook authentication token hardcoded and committed in appsettings.json
findings.rationale: Token is non-confidential by design: AddWebhook.razor pre-fills it into a public unauthenticated form, WebhooksSender echoes it to subscriber servers, and with ValidateToken unset the identical forgery is achievable without any token. Max impact is escaped-text rows in a display-only demo grid.

findings.title: RequireHttpsMetadata=false in all builds for API token validation and OIDC clients allows attacker-fed discovery/JWKS over HTTP
findings.rationale: Flag is unconditional but inert where it matters: AppHost.cs:22 defaults the https launch profile and injects the https identity endpoint into every consumer, so discovery/JWKS go over TLS; the http profile is the ESHOP_USE_HTTP_ENDPOINTS test-only mode; the counterfeit-JWKS attack additionally requires an internal MITM/DNS foothold the stated environment excludes. Hardening-only.

findings.title: Catalog decrements arbitrary product stock directly from forged event payload (ProductId/Units) with no order validation or dedup
findings.rationale: Handler mechanics accurate but every exploit path requires RabbitMQ publish access - an elevated precondition (internal foothold); the sole legitimate publisher builds events server-side from validated order lines; unsigned internal bus with network-as-trust-boundary is the intended architecture; the poison/ack sub-claim duplicates f049. Note: catalog stock can also be zeroed via the confirmed anonymous f003 CRUD, which is the internet-reachable version of this impact.

findings.title: Ordering.API integration-event handlers transition arbitrary orders based solely on event payload OrderId
findings.rationale: Handlers trust payload OrderId with no origin check (verified), but the first link in the attack chain is broker publish access - an elevated precondition; with that foothold the attacker already holds first-party publish credentials on the shared exchange, so message signing is defense-in-depth against an already-compromised actor. One dissent accepted the elevated precondition and confirmed the financial-fraud chain.

findings.title: Personal access token passed as command-line argument to az CLI, exposed via process listing
findings.rationale: No secret exists in source - patToken is a mandatory runtime operator parameter (rule 8); the script is dead legacy code referencing Dockerfiles that no longer exist (zero Dockerfiles repo-wide) with zero CI references; process-argv exposure requires a local foothold on the operator host. Hygiene recommendation only.

findings.title: Gateway endpoints default to and are persisted as http:// with no scheme validation; tokens ride cleartext and OIDC authority is user/tamper-controllable
findings.rationale: Endpoints are a deliberate user-editable settings surface (SettingsView.xaml:126-163); platform network-security configs restrict cleartext to 10.0.2.2/localhost; the tamperer scenario presupposes root/backup access that already grants stronger options; tokens live in SecureStorage and UseMocks defaults on. Hardening guidance (https-by-default, scheme validation), not an exploitable path.

findings.title: DEBUG Android HTTP handler accepts any self-signed cert with Issuer CN=localhost, ignoring chain errors
findings.rationale: #if DEBUG registration compiles out of release builds (GetKeyedService returns null, default validation restored); deliberate Microsoft-documented dev-cert pattern for loopback endpoints that never traverse hostile networks. Dissent: host-agnostic CN=localhost check exceeds the localhost-scoped intent shown in the iOS branch, and debug builds pointed at remote deployments is a routine workflow. Precision: dropped.

findings.title: iOS DEBUG TrustOverrideForUrl uses unanchored prefix match "https://localhost"
findings.rationale: Unanchored StartsWith confirmed but DEBUG-only, default endpoint is https://localhost:5243 (loopback, un-MITM-able), no writer of the endpoint setting exists other than the device owner's own Settings UI, and the OIDC authorization step runs through WebAuthenticator with normal TLS validation so the token-theft chain cannot self-sustain. Trigger requires the user to self-configure an attacker-controlled https://localhost* host.

findings.title: Antiforgery runs before HTTPS redirection; cookie Secure flag dependent on forwarded-proto trust
findings.rationale: Ordering is real but causally irrelevant: a plaintext POST is on the wire before any server middleware runs, so reordering UseHttpsRedirection changes nothing about wire exposure; the http listener exists only under the test-only ESHOP_USE_HTTP_ENDPOINTS profile; default https topology + ACA TLS termination makes SameAsRequest cookies Secure; HSTS in non-dev blocks repeat-visit http POSTs. Hardening suggestions only.

findings.title: Webhook subscription tokens stored in plaintext in PostgreSQL
findings.rationale: Token is user-supplied at registration and echoed back to its owner via GET; it must be recoverable verbatim for the X-eshop-whtoken header so hashing is impossible; it is already logged in cleartext elsewhere (GrantUrlTesterService.cs:17), so at-rest encryption closes no gap in this codebase; no attacker-reachable path to webhooksdb (parameterized EF Core throughout, internal network). Defense-in-depth only; one dissent treated CWE-312 as valid with the standard DB-foothold precondition.

findings.title: OpenAPI documents served unauthenticated in all environments; docs advertise deprecated implicit OAuth flow
findings.rationale: MapOpenApi ungated and the implicit-flow doc confirmed, but Ordering/Catalog/Webhooks APIs are internal-only (no WithExternalHttpEndpoints) and the internet-facing YARP BFF proxies only /catalog-api, /api/catalog/*, /api/orders/*, /identity/* — /openapi/v1.json is not externally routed. Exposure requires an internal foothold where the doc adds nothing; the repo's own THREAT_MODEL marks this risk_accepted.

findings.title: Catalog "stock validation" handler confirms stock for arbitrary OrderIds and silently treats missing products as in-stock
findings.rationale: Handler is broker-only (AddSubscription); exploit requires broker publish access (elevated precondition) and with it the attacker achieves the identical end state by publishing OrderStockConfirmedIntegrationEvent directly to Ordering.API — the Catalog round-trip adds zero marginal capability. Aggregate guard caps impact to orders genuinely in AwaitingValidation. Bus-trust is intended design; the root-cause trust issue is the separately-filed Ordering handler finding.

findings.title: android:allowBackup="true" backs up plaintext Preferences (OIDC authority, gateway URLs, client secret) enabling settings-tamper restore
findings.rationale: allowBackup=true confirmed but adds no capability: anyone with the required unlocked-device access can repoint endpoints through the app's own Settings UI (same Preferences keys); ClientSecret is the public constant "secret"; tokens are in SecureStorage (Keystore-bound, undecryptable on restore); adb backup of non-debuggable apps targeting Android 12+ excludes app data; cloud restore requires the victim's Google account. Intended configurability + missing hardening only.

findings.title: iOS NSAllowsLocalNetworking=true permits cleartext to LAN hosts where the default gateway endpoints live
findings.rationale: NSAllowsLocalNetworking=true ungated but iOS defaults are loopback (traffic never leaves the device), UseMocks defaults on (zero network calls), the only writer of gateway endpoints is the local Settings UI, and NSAllowsLocalNetworking is the scoped Apple mechanism enabling the app's documented local-container deployment mode. MITM requires the operator to voluntarily type an http:// LAN gateway on hostile Wi-Fi — trusted operator input (rule 8 territory).

findings.title: Consumer swallows all handler exceptions and acknowledges every message - poison events cause silent event loss
findings.rationale: Ack-always/no-DLX confirmed but the poison-interleaving attack is mechanically invalid: RabbitMQ delivers each message independently in a fresh DI scope (lines 190-207), so a poison message only destroys itself and the genuine event behind it is still processed. Suppressing a genuine event requires consume/admin capability, and an actor with broker publish access already holds strictly stronger primitives (forged-valid events). The behavior is explicitly documented as an intended sample trade-off (comment 177-179).

findings.title: Missing "Identity" config section silently disables all authentication and authorization for a service
findings.rationale: Early return confirmed but unreachable in shipped configurations: all three consumers bake an Identity section into appsettings.json, configuration layering means env vars can only add/override (never remove) a file-defined section, a merely-missing Identity__Url env var throws at GetRequiredValue (fail-loud), and no chart/profile artifact exists in the repo to strip the section. Line 26 documents the opt-in design; requires a trusted operator to edit appsettings inside the image.

findings.title: webapp confidential client disables PKCE on the authorization-code flow
findings.rationale: RequirePkce=false confirmed, but the sole webapp consumer is the ASP.NET Core OIDC handler which sends PKCE by default on .NET 8+ (never disabled in-repo), so every normal-flow code is bound to a challenge; the cited interception channels are dead (referrer policy strips cross-origin codes, /signin-oidc renders no content) and codes are single-use with a short lifetime. Exploitation requires an attacker-crafted PKCE-less authorize URL plus phishing plus a code-consumption race. One dissent kept it as a genuine but hard-to-trigger LOW.

findings.title: PAN masking runs before validation and throws unhandled for CardNumber shorter than 4 chars or null
findings.rationale: Exception before Mediator.Send so no side effects; production surfaces a sanitized 500 ProblemDetails with no disclosure; the endpoint's normal validation failures already produce the identical exception-to-500 path, so the marginal security difference is zero. Authenticated-user log noise / status-code nicety only.

findings.title: Forged paid/shipped events are fanned out to all webhook subscribers with valid tokens and attacker-controlled payload
findings.rationale: Fan-out mechanics verified but the only trigger is broker publish access (elevated precondition); with a foothold the attacker can already forge events at every bus consumer, so this is system-wide trusted-bus design rather than a Webhooks.API defect; the in-repo receiver just displays spoofed rows (nuisance). One dissent: Webhooks.API is the service that converts an internal forgery into externally-visible token-authenticated deliveries, a materialized blast-radius extension.

findings.title: RabbitMQ and Redis are provisioned without explicit authentication parameters; network-adjacent callers can forge integration events and read/rewrite any basket
findings.rationale: AddRabbitMQ auto-generates random credentials when none are supplied (no guest/open); every bus-participating container already holds working broker credentials injected via WithReference, so a foothold grants the same capability without this line; redis/eventbus have no public ingress in ACA or local topology; passwordless Redis east-west access is post-compromise exposure only (hardening).

findings.title: AppHost forces ASPNETCORE_FORWARDEDHEADERS_ENABLED=true on all projects, enabling client-supplied X-Forwarded-* spoofing that bypasses an IP gate
findings.rationale: The auto-injected ForwardedHeaders middleware uses the parameterless options (loopback known-proxy defaults) and applies headers only when the immediate peer is a known proxy, so an internet client's X-Forwarded-For is discarded and RemoteIpAddress is not rewritten; the sole RemoteIpAddress consumer is the [Authorize] diagnostics page rendering the caller's OWN claims - nothing gained. Nuisance/impact-free.

findings.title: CI actions pinned to mutable major tags; unpinned npm global install in workflow
findings.rationale: Mutable tags and unpinned npm confirmed, but no pull_request_target, zero secrets referenced by executed workflows (demo creds are plaintext, not secrets), markdownlint.yml pins permissions to contents:read, and the only artifact is a test report. The trigger requires compromising GitHub's actions org or an npm publisher - ecosystem event, not a repo vector. SHA-pinning is hardening advice.

findings.title: CI uploads Playwright report artifact containing authenticated-session traces for 30 days
findings.rationale: Traces do contain authenticated-session data, but the app-under-test is a fresh per-job AppHost stack on the runner (identitydb/Postgres/Redis are runner-local containers that die with the job) and the WebApp cookie is keyed to per-instance DataProtection - nothing survives to replay against. The captured credential (bob/Pass123$) is already public in the same repo and printed on the login page, granting zero incremental access.

findings.title: AndroidManifest ships usesCleartextTraffic="true"; network_security_config carve-out allows cleartext to 10.0.2.2
findings.rationale: NSC supersedes the manifest flag on modern targetSdk so real devices permit zero cleartext; the sole carve-out 10.0.2.2 is the emulator's host-loopback alias documented as intentional MAUI dev scaffolding, and the traffic never leaves the dev machine - capturing it requires owning the dev host (trusted operator). Mocks default on and stored endpoint prefs default empty.

findings.title: "throw-fake-exception" magic string in the message body suppresses all event processing
findings.rationale: Zero marginal capability: any malformed body traverses the identical catch-ack path, so an actor with broker access suppresses events with or without the string; publishing a poisoned message drops the poisoned message itself (FIFO), never a queued legit event. The only internet-reachable carrier (BuyerName into event bodies) drops only events about the attacker's own order - self-DoS nuisance. Overt debug scaffolding since the initial commit.

findings.title: ExternalController.Challenge accepts arbitrary caller-supplied authentication scheme and later trusts it as the identity-provider label
findings.rationale: Dormant and structurally impossible as claimed: Identity.API registers zero external providers (only cookie schemes), an unregistered scheme throws at Challenge and a cookie scheme never writes the idsrv.external temp cookie, so Callback's gate always throws and lines 151/155/213 are unreachable; even with a provider registered, the same scheme string drives both the challenge target and the stored label, so provider-A-authenticated / provider-B-labeled confusion cannot occur. Stock IdentityServer quickstart design.

findings.title: Diagnostics endpoint dumps all session claims and cookie properties behind an unreliable localhost IP check
findings.rationale: Decisive: the page renders HttpContext.AuthenticateAsync() - the auth-cookie principal, which contains only id/username/security-stamp/email/roles - NOT the token claims; card_number/card_security_number/address claims are emitted only into issued tokens via ProfileService and never enter the browser cookie, so the claimed card-data dump cannot occur on any path. [Authorize] means self-disclosure only; RemoteIpAddress is the TCP peer and spoofability is contested (no app-level forwarded-headers middleware; even granting it, impact is zero). Verbatim IdentityServer quickstart template.

findings.title: Outbox events stranded in InProgress/Failed states are never republished - broker fault injection silently kills events
findings.rationale: No sweeper confirmed, but every publish is wrapped in a Polly retry pipeline (RetryCount=10, exponential backoff) covering BrokerUnreachableException/SocketException - a one-shot injected connection reset lands on retry; stranding requires sustained internal-broker outage or a precise crash window (elevated precondition, non-adversarial); HTTP client aborts do not cancel the publish (no RequestAborted usage). Reliability/at-least-once resiliency gap, no attacker gain.

findings.title: Postgres superuser credentials with weak placeholder password checked in across five services' config
findings.rationale: Deliberately fake, CredScan-suppressed-as-Dummy placeholder in Development-only localhost config; the supported topology injects Aspire-generated connection strings via WithReference env vars that override the JSON at the sole consumer (GetConnectionString), so the value is dead config; no compose/k8s artifact references it; the exploit is a two-step operator-error hypothetical (promote dev file to prod AND expose postgres).

findings.title: Circuit-bound identity snapshots: ChatState captures the user principal once and user-scoped calls ride a token resolved from ambient HttpContext
findings.rationale: The trigger cannot occur: logout is a static-SSR form post that signs out and issues a cross-origin redirect to the separate identity-api IdP - a full page load destroying the circuit; re-login round-trips the same IdP and creates a fresh circuit/user snapshot. Stale IHttpContextAccessor on circuits yields a null token that fails closed (unauthenticated GetBasket returns empty; UpdateBasket throws Unauthenticated). Anyone at the abandoned unlocked browser already holds the live session cookie, so the stale chat snapshot grants nothing. Missing RevalidatingServerAuthenticationStateProvider is hardening only.

findings.title: SaveTokens persists the IdP access token inside the auth cookie, which the relay then distributes to every backend
findings.rationale: The token sits inside the DataProtection-encrypted cookie ticket (no ITicketStore/custom TicketDataFormat anywhere), so a cookie thief holds an opaque blob and cannot extract the token without the server's DataProtection keys - a compromise that already permits forging cookies for any user. Whole-cookie replay already achieves the identical ceiling through the app's own relay (which attaches the same token to the same backend calls). SaveTokens + bearer forwarding is the canonical OIDC-client pattern here.

findings.title: Unauthenticated MapForwarder relays attacker-shaped {id} into the catalog-api request path
findings.rationale: Structurally dead: /product-images/{id} is a single-segment template and Kestrel percent-decodes the path before routing, so %2e%2e%2f decodes into three segments and never matches the 2-segment pattern - the forwarder never fires and {id} can never contain a slash. Even a literal .. segment canonicalizes to a nonexistent route and every catalog-api destination is :int-constrained; the destination host is pinned to catalog-api. Path-only shaping at most; the pic endpoint is deliberately public.

findings.title: sub-less access tokens create subscriptions owned by NULL user id, forming a shared pseudo-tenant namespace
findings.rationale: No sub-less token is mintable: identity-api's only clients are GrantTypes.Code/Implicit user-delegation flows (always include sub), the relay forwards user tokens, and the JWT bearer pins the authority to identity-api so no external sub-less token is accepted. Even granting one, UserId is [Required] on the model so the write path fails. Defense-in-depth null-guard hardening only.

findings.title: Attacker-settable stored PictureFileName is resolved to a file with no format allowlist; served MIME type is derived from the attacker-chosen extension
findings.rationale: Live-today step yields nothing: Pics contains exactly 101 repo-shipped .webp product images that are already anonymously served, so pointing an item at one discloses nothing. The harmful SVG/content-type chain requires attacker-writable bytes in Pics and repo-wide grep finds no write path; the .svg/.wmf MIME entries are declared intended API surface (ProducedProducesResponseType).

findings.title: Unauthenticated OPTIONS /check reflects arbitrary attacker header value into the response header
findings.rationale: The echo is the designed grant handshake: GrantUrlTesterService sends OPTIONS with the token and grants only when the receiver echoes it back, asserted by the unit test. Kestrel rejects CR/LF/NUL inbound and validates on write; no caching middleware exists; only the requester observes the reflection. Hypothetical misbehaving-intermediary scenario only.

findings.title: DEBUG build ships an extra trusted issuer "https://10.0.2.2:5243"
findings.rationale: JwtBearer still validates signatures against the Authority's JWKS regardless of the extra issuer string; JWKS publishes only public keys so 'obtaining a key from it' confers nothing, and holding the real private signing key is full IdP compromise at which point tokens with the legitimate iss pass in Release too - the DEBUG issuer adds zero marginal capability. No Dockerfiles exist for debug-binary drift.
